root_cause_short: Unreleased EMN bonding-curve token contracts were discovered on-chain and manipulated via flash loans, minting/burning against the bonding curve to extract reserve DAI.
exploit_steps: Identify unreleased Eminence contracts already deployed and holding DAI
Take a flash loan of DAI
Buy EMN against the bonding curve, inflating its price
Mint sub-token (eAAVE) using EMN, shifting reserves
Burn EMN back to DAI at the favorable manipulated curve price
Repay flash loan and keep the surplus DAI
invariant_broken: Bonding-curve reserve value must equal sum of outstanding token claims; partial burns across nested tokens must not let total redeemable value exceed reserves.
prerequisites: Unaudited contracts deployed with funds before public launch
notes: Andre Cronje's experimental project; attacker returned ~$8M to Cronje who redistributed it. Loss often cited as $15M total drained.

root_cause_short: Vault share price derived from Curve y-pool spot balances; flash loans temporarily skewed stablecoin prices so deposits/withdrawals minted/redeemed shares at distorted value.
exploit_steps: Take a large USDT/USDC flash loan
Swap USDC to USDT in Curve y-pool to push USDT price up
Deposit USDT into Harvest vault at depressed share price
Swap USDT back to USDC to push USDT price down
Withdraw from vault, redeeming shares for more USDT than deposited
Repeat ~32 cycles and exit via renBTC and Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Vault share price must be immune to single-transaction manipulation of the underlying AMM spot price.
notes: ~$33.8M total moved out of FARM_USDT/FARM_USDC pools; attacker's net take ~$24M. Attacker returned ~$2.48M. Harvest framed it as an 'arbitrage economic attack'.

root_cause_short: Deposit credited the user based on before/after balance difference; a malicious token re-entered deposit during transfer, getting double-credited.
exploit_steps: Deploy a malicious ERC20 token with a callback in transferFrom
Call the pool deposit function with the fake token
During transfer, re-enter deposit to deposit real DAI and get credited
Outer deposit also credits the same DAI (double counting)
Withdraw DAI for more than deposited
Repeat in ~$50k batches using a flash loan to reach ~$2M
invariant_broken: Deposit accounting must not double-count value when the token transfer can re-enter the deposit function.
notes: Contracts had been audited by SmartDec and Certik. Attack contract 0xe2307837524db8961c4541f943598654240bd62f.

root_cause_short: Vault used Curve spot price as oracle and used the wrong Curve math function on withdrawal; flash-loan manipulation let attacker withdraw excess via the Vault/Proxy path.
exploit_steps: Take a large flash loan
Deposit into the Value DeFi vault
Manipulate the Curve spot price used as oracle
Withdraw through the Vault/Proxy path using the mispriced Curve math
Redeem for more than deposited
Repay flash loan and keep surplus
invariant_broken: Collateral/share valuation must not rely on a manipulable AMM spot price reachable within one transaction.
prerequisites: Curve spot price used as oracle
notes: Attacker returned ~$2M as a 'good faith' gesture with a note. Hit ~20 min before a scheduled AMA.

root_cause_short: OUSD mint function performed token transfer-in before updating supply/rebase accounting, allowing a reentrant malicious token to mint OUSD without backing.
exploit_steps: Take flash loans of stablecoins (DAI/USDT)
Call OUSD mintMultiple including a malicious token
During the malicious token transfer, re-enter mint
Trigger rebase so attacker's OUSD balance inflates
Redeem inflated OUSD for the vault's real stablecoins
Repay flash loans and exit via Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Total OUSD supply must always be fully backed; mint accounting must complete before any external call.
notes: rekt leaderboard lists ~$8M ('Hack Epidemic / Origin Protocol'); DeFiLlama ~$7M. Reentrancy combined with rebasing supply logic.

root_cause_short: ControllerV4's swapExactJarForJar did not whitelist jars, letting a fake malicious Jar be swapped against the legitimate cDAI jar to drain it.
exploit_steps: Deploy a fake malicious Pickle Jar
Call swapExactJarForJar with the legit cDAI jar and the fake jar
Because jars are not whitelisted, the swap moves funds into the fake jar
Drain ~19.7M DAI from the cDAI jar into attacker control
invariant_broken: Inter-jar swaps must only operate on protocol-whitelisted, trusted jar contracts.
prerequisites: swapExactJarForJar callable with arbitrary jar addresses
notes: Vulnerable ControllerV4 (Oct 23) was deployed after MixBytes/Haechi audits and was out of their scope. White-hat war room rescued remaining ~$50M at risk.

root_cause_short: Uniswap WETH-DAI LP token used as collateral was valued via the manipulable AMM spot price; flash loans inflated LP value to over-borrow.
exploit_steps: Take flash loans (~2.9M DAI + ~345K WETH) from dYdX and Uniswap pairs
Deposit DAI+WETH into Uniswap WETH-DAI to mint LP tokens
Deposit LP tokens into WarpVaultLP as collateral
Swap large WETH for DAI to inflate DAI price and roughly double LP token value
Borrow ~3.86M DAI + ~3.9M USDC against inflated collateral
Repay flash loans, leaving an underwater position
invariant_broken: LP collateral valuation must reflect manipulation-resistant fair price, not instantaneous reserves.
prerequisites: LP token priced via AMM spot reserves
notes: A portion (~$5.5M) recovered as attacker's borrow left ~94,349 LP tokens locked/liquidatable. Funded via Tornado Cash.

root_cause_short: Blacksmith staking contract had a storage/memory bug; leaving 1 wei of LP balance and re-depositing triggered massively inflated COVER reward minting.
exploit_steps: Stake Balancer Pool Tokens (BPT) into Blacksmith
Withdraw nearly all, leaving 1 wei balance
Become effectively sole LP for the pool
Re-deposit BPT
Claim rewards; bug mints quintillions of COVER
Sell minted COVER via 1inch and extract value
invariant_broken: Reward minting must be bounded by actual stake and elapsed time; storage and memory copies of accounting structs must not diverge.
notes: $9.4M taken, ~$3.2M recovered. Grap Finance returned 4,351 ETH claiming whitehat status; rekt expressed skepticism. Six addresses used the loophole.

root_cause_short: Alpha Homora V2's empty sUSD pool plus a rounding flaw let totalDebt be inflated without increasing totalDebtShare, so the attacker borrowed huge sums treated as near-zero debt shares.
exploit_steps: Become sole borrower of the empty sUSD pool via a custom 'evil spell'
Repay 1 wei less than total debt, leaving 1 debt share
Call resolveReserve to inflate totalDebt while totalDebtShare stays 1
Repeatedly borrow amounts 1 less than totalDebt so computed debt share rounds to 0
Use Aave/Cream flash loans to scale sUSD borrows and double each round
Convert borrowed assets to aTokens/Curve LP and launder via Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Debt shares must be monotonically consistent with totalDebt; borrowing must always increase a borrower's recorded debt share.
notes: Hit Cream's Iron Bank via Alpha Homora V2. Alpha cited a 'prime suspect' and insider-knowledge-level complexity. Attacker sent 1k ETH each to Cream and Alpha deployers.

root_cause_short: Attacker compromised a machine and stole the single admin mnemonic; with no multisig or timelock, an unrestricted transfer function drained treasury liquidity and EASY tokens.
exploit_steps: Compromise the founder's machine holding the admin mnemonic
Derive private keys for the admin account
Call the unrestricted transfer function (no timelock)
Drain ~$6M stablecoins and ~$53M EASY tokens (~30% of supply)
invariant_broken: Privileged treasury operations must require multisig/timelock and never be controllable by a single compromised key.
notes: rekt/DeFiLlama figure ~$59M (mostly illiquid EASY); ~$6M was liquid stablecoins. Compared by founder to the Nexus Mutual machine-compromise incident.

root_cause_short: During v2 migration, the balance-check multiplier was changed from 1000 to 10000 in only some places, breaking the x*y=k check so 1 wei could swap for ~98% of reserves.
exploit_steps: Send minimal amounts of each token to the pair contracts
Call the low-level swap() function
Exploit the broken k-check to swap ~1 wei input for ~98% of the output reserve
Drain reserves across WBNB, BUSD, ETH, BTC, DOT, ADA, USDT, U92
Launder portions through Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: After every swap, reserve product k must not decrease (x*y=k must hold with consistent scaling constants).
prerequisites: Buggy migrated pair contract live with liquidity
notes: Bug appeared during migration and was exploited right before the planned v2.1 fix; the GitHub repo was removed, raising insider-insertion suspicions. A separate earlier MasterChef exploit also occurred that month.

root_cause_short: calcLiquidityShare() read current pool balance instead of a cached balance, so inflating the balance before burning LP tokens returned more assets than deposited.
exploit_steps: Take a 10K WBNB flash loan
Swap WBNB to SPARTA repeatedly through the vulnerable pool
Add SPARTA+WBNB as liquidity, minting pool tokens
Transfer extra WBNB and SPARTA directly into the pool to inflate its balance
Burn the earlier pool tokens; inflated balance returns excess assets
Repeat to drain, then repay the flash loan
invariant_broken: LP redemption value must be computed from cached accounted reserves, not externally manipulable current token balances.
notes: Funds laundered via 1inch, Nerve, Anyswap; exited as ~219.5 BTC and ~3311 ETH. Slippage reduced realized profit by ~1/3.

root_cause_short: BvaultsStrategy mishandled the difference between BUSD (18 decimals) and the underlying, letting an attacker exploit deposit/withdraw share accounting to drain vault funds.
exploit_steps: Take a flash loan of BUSD
Interact with the BvaultsStrategy deposit/withdraw flow
Exploit the decimal/share accounting discrepancy to over-redeem
Drain BUSD from the vault
Repay flash loan and keep surplus
invariant_broken: Vault share-to-asset conversion must be exact across differing token decimals and not allow net value extraction via deposit/withdraw.
notes: rekt/DeFiLlama figure ~$18M from the BUSD vault. Occurred during the May 2021 BSC flash-loan wave.

root_cause_short: VaultFlipToFlip valued LP/reward using PancakeSwap spot prices; flash loans skewed the WBNB-BUSDT pool so getReward minted ~6.97M BUNNY, which was dumped.
exploit_steps: Take 8 flash loans (WBNB from several PancakeSwap pools + USDT from Fortube)
Add USDT+WBNB liquidity to the WBNB-BUSDT pool
Swap large WBNB for BUSDT to skew reserves and inflate LP valuation
Call getReward() on VaultFlipToFlip to mint ~6.97M BUNNY at the distorted valuation
Dump BUNNY, crashing price from ~$146 to ~$6
Repay all flash loans
invariant_broken: Reward minting tied to LP value must use a manipulation-resistant price, not single-tx AMM spot reserves.
prerequisites: AMM spot price used for reward valuation
notes: Loot wallet 0xa0acc61547f6bd066f7c9663c17a312b6ad7e187. Haechi-audited project, but the exploited new code was outside audit scope. A second smaller PancakeBunny (Polygon, $2.4M) occurred July 2021.

root_cause_short: Uniswap-fork pair omitted the x*y=k check and allowed reentrancy, letting a fake token pair be used to swap for large output while paying ~1 unit input.
exploit_steps: Flash swap ~6k WBNB from PancakeSwap
Swap nearly all WBNB to BURGER on BurgerSwap
Create a fake BEP-20 token and pair it with BURGER
Swap the fake tokens to WBNB exploiting the missing k-check and reentrancy
Repeat across 14 transactions to extract assets
Repay the flash swap and keep profit
invariant_broken: Every swap must preserve the constant product k and complete reserve updates before any reentrant call.
notes: Taken in 14 transactions (~$7.2M). x*y=k check present in univ2pair was removed in this fork.

root_cause_short: Belt valued multi-strategy vault shares assuming all strategies stay balanced; flash loans unbalanced the Venus/Ellipsis strategies to over-redeem on withdrawal.
exploit_steps: Take a flash loan
Deposit heavily into the undersubscribed Venus strategy to make it oversubscribed
Unbalance the 3eps pool by swapping BUSD to USDT via Ellipsis
Vault overestimates share value due to imbalance
Withdraw BUSD from the Venus strategy for more than deposited
Repeat ~7 times (~$1M each) and repay flash loan
invariant_broken: Vault share valuation must be correct under arbitrary strategy imbalance, not assume balanced pools.
prerequisites: Share value derived from one strategy's pool
notes: ~$6.3M drained; team had claimed the attack pattern was 'impossible' with their protocol.

root_cause_short: The V3 Router's MPC signing reused the same ECDSA k (nonce) across two BSC transactions, allowing the private key to be back-calculated and bridge liquidity drained.
exploit_steps: Observe V3 Router signatures on BSC
Detect two transactions sharing the same ECDSA k value
Back-calculate the signing private key from the repeated nonce
Use the recovered key to drain V3 liquidity pools across chains
invariant_broken: Every ECDSA signature must use a unique random nonce k; nonce reuse must never occur.
notes: Stolen: ~5.5M MIM + ~2.4M USDC across Ethereum, BSC, Fantom. Only new V3 pools affected; V1/V2 bridge stayed operational. Known issue documented since 2010.

root_cause_short: The per-token proxy Factory's mint authorization could be bypassed by supplying a fresh address as the signature, letting the attacker mint bridged tokens to arbitrary addresses.
exploit_steps: Call the receive/mint function on the Factory contract
Bypass the auth check by using a new address as the signature each call
Pay the small chargeFee and set destination to attacker address
Mint tokens repeatedly across ~20 tokens
Sell minted tokens (e.g. WILD/WBNB on PancakeSwap) and bridge ETH out via 1inch
invariant_broken: Cross-chain mints must require a valid signature from the authorized signer over the specific mint payload.
prerequisites: Weak/spoofable signature verification in Factory contracts
notes: Second ChainSwap incident in July 2021 (~$4.4M); a first incident days earlier cost ~$800k. Affected ~20 tokens on Ethereum and BSC. Attacker ETH address 0xEda5066780dE29D00dfb54581A707ef6F52D8113.

root_cause_short: A fake router/Asgard contract and malformed memo made Bifrost misread a forwarded ETH transfer as a legitimate deposit, triggering an erroneous refund to the attacker.
exploit_steps: Deploy a fake router contract
Send ETH to trigger a deposit event
Call returnVaultAssets() defining the fake router as an Asgard vault
Real THORChain router forwards ETH to the fake Asgard, creating a fraudulent deposit event with a malicious memo
Bifrost reads it as a normal deposit and refunds the attacker
invariant_broken: Bifrost must only credit deposits from genuine vault flows and validate memo/source authenticity before refunding.
prerequisites: Bifrost trusts event+memo without strict source validation
notes: Second THORChain attack of July 2021 (~$8M: ALCX, XRUNE, USDC, SUSHI, YFI, USDT); a first ~$5M attack occurred ~July 15. Attacker reportedly motivated 'for power, not wealth'. Analysis by Halborn and Mudit Gupta. (Note: a same-cluster sibling incident was not independently verified for inclusion; dangling link removed.)

root_cause_short: EthCrossChainManager could call any contract it owned; via a sighash collision the attacker invoked putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes on EthCrossChainData to replace the keeper public keys and seize control.
exploit_steps: Craft cross-chain input whose function selector collides (first 4 bytes 0x41973cd9) with putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes
Submit via verifyHeaderAndExecuteTx so the manager calls executeCrossChainTx
Target the manager-owned EthCrossChainData contract, passing the onlyOwner check
Replace the keeper/consensus public keys with attacker-controlled keys
Authorize and execute withdrawals draining assets on Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon
invariant_broken: Cross-chain relay execution must never be able to call privileged self-owned management/data contracts.
notes: Largest DeFi hack at the time (~$611M). Attacker ('Mr. White Hat') returned essentially all funds after dialogue; Tether froze ~33M USDT. No private key was compromised.

root_cause_short: Cream's lending market for AMP (an ERC777-style token) allowed a reentrant borrow during the token transfer callback, letting the attacker borrow twice against the same collateral.
exploit_steps: Supply collateral and borrow AMP from the Cream market
During the AMP transfer hook, re-enter and borrow ETH again before state updates
Repeat the reentrant borrow to extract more than collateral allows
Walk away with the borrowed ETH
invariant_broken: Borrow accounting must update before any external token-transfer callback (no reentrant borrow).
prerequisites: ERC777-style token with transfer callback listed as collateral/borrowable
notes: First of Cream's two 2021 hacks (~$18.8M via AMP reentrancy). Distinct from the October 2021 oracle exploit.

root_cause_short: Vee used a single-source Pangolin spot price without decimal processing, so price manipulation on a thin pair bypassed slippage checks during leveraged trades.
exploit_steps: Fund Avalanche wallet via Tornado Cash bridging
Create thin swap pairs (e.g. QI/WETH.e) on Pangolin
Deploy a dynamic exploit contract for leveraged trading
Manipulate the Pangolin reference price on the QI/WETH.e pair
Open leveraged positions that bypass slippage control due to missing decimals
Extract value as USDT.e/WETH.e and bridge back to Ethereum
invariant_broken: Leveraged-trade pricing must use a manipulation-resistant oracle with correct decimal handling and enforce slippage bounds.
notes: Attacker's ETH wallet ended with ~214 WBTC and ~8,804 WETH. Vee had Slowmist and Certik audits. Second major Avalanche loss that month.

root_cause_short: PriceOracleProxy valued yUSDVault collateral by pricePerShare (balance/totalSupply); redeeming most supply then donating tokens roughly doubled per-share value, inflating collateral.
exploit_steps: Use MakerDAO and Aave flash loans across two coordinated addresses to mint large crYUSD and yUSDVault positions
Loop deposits/borrows to accumulate ~$1.5B crYUSD and ~$500M yUSDVault
Redeem ~$500M yUSDVault to shrink totalSupply to ~$8M
Deposit ~$8M yUSD back, roughly doubling per-share value
Cream revalues collateral to ~$3B; withdraw assets to repay loans
Drain Cream's remaining ~$130M lending assets and launder via Tornado/renBridge
invariant_broken: Collateral share price must not be manipulable by changing vault totalSupply within a transaction.
notes: Cream's largest hack (~$130M); third major Cream incident overall. Exploit input contained taunts referencing rivals; analysts suspected an experienced DeFi dev.

root_cause_short: swapTokenForExactToken allowed the same token as tokenIn and tokenOut; swapping MONO against itself overwrote tokenIn price with the inflated tokenOut price.
exploit_steps: Call swapTokenForExactToken with MONO as both tokenIn and tokenOut
Each self-swap overwrites tokenIn price with the higher tokenOut price
Repeat to inflate MONO's price dramatically
Use the overvalued MONO to buy all other assets in the single-token pools
Repeat the same attack on Ethereum ~17 minutes later
invariant_broken: A swap must not use the same asset for input and output; price updates must not let a token inflate its own price.
notes: ~$19.4M on Polygon + ~$12M on Ethereum. Audited by Halborn and Peckshield. Stolen assets included MATIC, WETH, WBTC, LINK, MIM, IMX.

root_cause_short: Attackers injected malicious token-approval transactions into Badger's compromised front-end, harvesting unlimited allowances and later draining user wallets directly.
exploit_steps: Compromise the Badger web front-end (reportedly via a Cloudflare account)
Inject hidden approval prompts into legitimate user deposit/claim transactions
Users unknowingly grant unlimited allowances to the attacker address
Accumulate approvals over ~12 days
Starting Dec 2 00:00 UTC, drain approved tokens from victim wallets
Bridge underlying BTC back to Bitcoin, hold remaining ERC20s on Ethereum
invariant_broken: Front-end-served transaction calldata must match the intended user action; no unexpected approvals should be injected.
prerequisites: Users approving from the dApp UI
notes: ~$120M in wBTC and ERC20s. Attacker address 0x1fcdb04d0c5364fbd92c73ca8af9baa72c269107 approved by 500+ addresses. A transferFrom feature caused malicious txns to start failing ~2h20m in.

root_cause_short: Private keys for 96 user custodial wallets (managed via the integrated Venly service) were compromised and the wallets drained.
exploit_steps: Obtain private keys of 96 Vulcan Forged user custodial wallets
Drain PYR, ETH, and MATIC from those wallets
Consolidate stolen assets into attacker wallets across Ethereum and Polygon
Begin selling PYR, pushing price down ~30%
invariant_broken: User custodial private keys must remain confidential and non-extractable from the custody service.
prerequisites: Custodial wallet integration with extractable keys
notes: ~$140M (>4.5M PYR). Hacker address 0x48ad05a3B73c9E7fAC5918857687d6A11d2c73B1 on both chains. Team reimbursed most affected wallets from treasury and pledged to remove custodial wallets.

root_cause_short: The vault's depositFor() lacked reentrancy protection and let users pass arbitrary deposit tokens, so a malicious token re-entered to loop fake deposits and inflate vault shares.
exploit_steps: Take a flash loan of two tokens and add liquidity on SpiritSwap to mint LP
Call depositFor() with attacker as token and user
Use the token's safeTransferFrom to re-enter depositFor()
Loop reentrant deposits, compounding minted vault tokens at each level
On final call deposit the real LP token
Withdraw inflated vault tokens, remove liquidity, repay flash loan
invariant_broken: Vault share minting must complete state updates before external token-transfer callbacks; deposit tokens must be trusted.
notes: Grim was a Beefy fork; GRIM dropped ~80%. Same vector reportedly hit Charge DeFi hours earlier (possible serial attacker).

root_cause_short: The vVISR/Visor supply deposit function failed to verify the caller against the recorded owner, letting the attacker mint reward shares and drain VISR.
exploit_steps: Call the vulnerable deposit function on the Visor reward contract
Pass attacker-controlled owner data that is not validated
Mint inflated vVISR shares without legitimate deposit
Redeem the shares to drain VISR tokens
invariant_broken: Deposit/mint must verify msg.sender matches the position owner before crediting shares.
prerequisites: Deposit function trusts caller-supplied owner without validation
notes: ~$8.2M in VISR drained via an owner-verification flaw in the staking/reward deposit path.

root_cause_short: Legacy deposit() left callable after depositETH() added; tokenAddress.safeTransferFrom did not revert on zero/null address, so attacker minted qXETH collateral on BSC without locking ETH on Ethereum.
exploit_steps: Fund attacker address via Tornado Cash
Call QBridge deposit() routing to QBridgeHandler with zero token address
safeTransferFrom does not revert with null tokenAddress, so no real deposit occurs
Mint ~77,162 qXETH collateral on BSC
Borrow WETH, BTC-B, stablecoins, CAKE, BUNNY, MDX against fake collateral
Swap borrowed assets into ~200k BNB
invariant_broken: Minted bridge collateral on destination chain must be backed 1:1 by assets actually locked/transferred on the source chain.
prerequisites: obsolete deposit() function still present and unguarded
handler configured with zero token address for native ETH
notes: Cross-chain X-collateral feature reportedly audited by Theori Dec 2021. Qubit offered max $250k Immunefi bounty. Funds laundered via Tornado Cash.

root_cause_short: Wormhole's Solana contract used a deprecated load_instruction_at that did not verify the sysvar instructions account, letting the attacker spoof the guardian SignatureSet and mint 120k whETH unbacked.
exploit_steps: Reuse a SignatureSet from an earlier transaction and call verify_signatures on the bridge
Exploit the deprecated instructions-sysvar check that fails to validate the address, supplying a Secp256k1 instruction backed by only ~0.1 ETH
Create a forged SignatureSet account
Call complete_wrapped to mint 120,000 whETH on Solana without collateral
Bridge 93,750 ETH back to Ethereum across three transactions
Sell remaining ~36k whETH on Solana for USDC and SOL
invariant_broken: whETH minted on Solana must be backed 1:1 by ETH locked in the Ethereum contract and authorized by a valid 2/3 guardian signature set.
prerequisites: use of deprecated solana_program instruction-loading function
ability to create arbitrary SignatureSet accounts
notes: Jump Crypto/Certus One replenished the 120k ETH within hours to keep whETH 1:1 backed. Attacker address 0x629e7da20197a5429d30da36e77d06cdf796b71a. $10M bounty offer went unanswered.

root_cause_short: Meter's fork of ChainSafe ChainBridge modified the ERC20 handler deposit logic for wrapped native tokens; the unguarded deposit() trusted an arbitrary amount in calldata without an actual token transfer, allowing minting of BNB/wETH.
exploit_steps: Call the unguarded deposit() method on the ERC20 handler
Supply an arbitrary amount in calldata that bypasses the missing transfer/lock check
Maliciously mint large amounts of BNB and wETH on the bridge
Drain the bridge reserves of BNB and wETH
Launder proceeds into Tornado Cash over ~1 hour
invariant_broken: Bridge-minted wrapped native tokens must equal the native tokens actually locked in the handler contract.
notes: ~$4.4M drained directly from Meter plus ~$3.3M collateral damage on Hundred Finance (Moonriver) via BNB.bsc depreciation arbitrage. Meter accepted responsibility and planned token reimbursement.

root_cause_short: Agave (Aave fork) on Gnosis Chain accepted a token whose _callAfterTransfer hook enabled reentrancy; attacker re-entered borrow before debt was recorded.
exploit_steps: Take flash loan as initial collateral
Trigger token transfer with _callAfterTransfer callback
Nest additional borrow calls inside the callback before debt balances update
Repeat to borrow far in excess of collateral
Repay flash loan and exit with profit, route funds to Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: A borrower's outstanding debt must be fully recorded before control returns to the borrower or further borrowing is allowed.
prerequisites: listed collateral token with transfer callback
no reentrancy guard in borrow path
notes: First major attack on Gnosis Chain (xDai). Same attacker/pattern hit Hundred Finance minutes later. ~2116 ETH lost.

root_cause_short: Deus lending used the manipulable Solidex/SpiritSwap sAMM USDC/DEI pool as collateral price oracle; attacker flash-loaned DEI to distort it and force liquidations.
exploit_steps: Flash loan ~9.7M DEI via SpiritSwap USDC/DEI pool
Flash loan ~24.8M DEI from the sAMM USDC/DEI pair used as the price oracle
Liquidate users rendered insolvent by the manipulated collateral price
Repay ~24.8M DEI to the oracle pair
Burn liquidated LP tokens to recover ~5.22M USDC + ~5.25M DEI
Swap USDC to DEI, repay loans, keep ~3M DEI profit
invariant_broken: Collateral valuation for liquidations must use a manipulation-resistant price, not an instantaneous single-pool spot price.
prerequisites: spot price from a single shallow AMM pool
notes: First of two 2022 Deus incidents. Proceeds bridged via Multichain to Ethereum and routed through Tornado Cash. Deus planned to reimburse liquidated users.

root_cause_short: Hundred Finance (Compound fork) on Gnosis Chain hit by the same callback reentrancy via xDai token _callAfterTransfer, allowing over-borrowing before debt updates.
exploit_steps: Take flash loan as initial collateral
Trigger token transfer invoking _callAfterTransfer
Nest borrow calls within the callback before borrow balances update
Borrow well beyond posted collateral
Repay flash loan, exit, route to Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Outstanding debt must be recorded before control returns to the caller or additional borrowing occurs.
notes: ~2363 ETH lost. Same attacker/pattern as Agave, occurred ~3 minutes apart. Pattern mirrors CREAM Finance reentrancy.

root_cause_short: Cashio's collateral validation never checked the LP token's .mint field, letting an attacker pass worthless fake collateral accounts and mint unlimited CASH stablecoin.
exploit_steps: Create a fake root contract that bypasses validation
Build a chain of fake accounts validating only against each other
Create a false bank to pass common.collateral verification
Deposit worthless token as collateral
Mint ~2 billion CASH against it
Redeem/swap CASH via Saber for ~26M USDC+UST and bridge to Ethereum into ~16k ETH
invariant_broken: Minted CASH must be fully backed by validated, genuine collateral whose mint authority matches the expected token.
notes: Attacker claimed via transaction memo to return accounts under $100k and donate the rest. Analysis credited to samczsun and others.

root_cause_short: Attacker compromised 5 of 9 Ronin validator keys (4 controlled by Sky Mavis plus a never-revoked Axie DAO gas-free RPC whitelist signature) and authorized fraudulent withdrawals.
exploit_steps: Compromise Sky Mavis's four validator signatures (via spearphishing)
Abuse the still-active Axie DAO gas-free RPC node whitelist to obtain the fifth signature
Reach 5-of-9 consensus on the bridge
Authorize two withdrawals draining 173,600 ETH and 25.5M USDC
Swap USDC to ETH and move funds through mixers/exchanges
invariant_broken: No single party should control a quorum of bridge validator signatures; withdrawal approvals must require independent honest validators.
notes: Discovered ~6 days later. Later attributed by US authorities to North Korea's Lazarus Group (not in rekt source). Threshold raised to 8/9 afterward.

root_cause_short: Inverse's Keep3r-routed SushiSwap TWAP oracle for INV used a thin INV-WETH pair; attacker spiked the price and borrowed against overvalued INV collateral.
exploit_steps: Withdraw 901 ETH from Tornado Cash and disperse to fresh addresses
Swap ~500 ETH for ~1.7k INV in the low-liquidity SushiSwap INV-WETH pair, spiking price ~50x
Spam transactions to land first in the next block and capture inflated TWAP
Oracle returns manipulated INV price
Deposit 1.7k INV (fair value ~$644k) as collateral
Borrow ~$15.6M (ETH, WBTC, DOLA, YFI) against it
invariant_broken: Collateral price must be resistant to single-block, single-pool manipulation before being used for borrowing limits.
prerequisites: TWAP from a shallow single DEX pair
ability to win block ordering / MEV control
notes: First of two 2022 Inverse incidents. Described as highly MEV-aware. Inverse planned a Chainlink INV feed.

root_cause_short: TRUNK stablecoin minting swapped BUSD->WBNB->ELEPHANT during mint, inflating ELEPHANT spot price; attacker used flash loans to cycle this and extract value.
exploit_steps: Flash loan ~131k WBNB and 91M BUSD
Swap WBNB to ~34.2e21 ELEPHANT
Mint TRUNK by depositing BUSD, whose mint path buys ELEPHANT and raises its price
Sell the appreciated ELEPHANT for more WBNB
Redeem TRUNK for WBNB+BUSD
Repay flash loans and repeat cycles (~$4M/cycle)
invariant_broken: Stablecoin mint/redeem must not let a caller profit from price impact their own mint causes on the backing token.
prerequisites: mint logic that market-buys the backing token at spot
notes: Project audited by Solidity Finance which did not flag the manipulation vector. Official post-mortem reported $11.2M; PeckShield's figure including ~30B ELEPHANT was $22.2M.

root_cause_short: Beanstalk on-chain governance had no execution timelock; attacker used flash-loaned liquidity to gain a supermajority and instantly pass a malicious proposal draining the protocol.
exploit_steps: Pre-submit malicious BIP-18 (and a decoy Ukraine-donation proposal) a day prior
Flash loan ~350M DAI, 500M USDC, 150M USDT, 32M BEAN, 11.6M LUSD
Add borrowed assets to Curve pools and deposit LP into Beanstalk Diamond for voting weight
Call emergencyCommit to instantly pass BIP-18
Malicious proposal transfers all protocol funds to attacker contract
Remove liquidity, repay flash loans, keep ~24,830 WETH
invariant_broken: Governance proposals must not be executable within a single transaction/flash-loan window; voting power should not be flash-loanable into instant execution.
prerequisites: voting power derivable from instantly-acquired LP
notes: Attacker net profit ~$76M after repaying loans; donated 250k USDC to Ukraine. Proceeds laundered via Tornado Cash. Auditor Omniscia said attack was out of audit scope.

root_cause_short: Second Deus incident: lending price oracle again derived from a manipulable DEI liquidity pool, enabling flash-loan price distortion and improper borrowing/liquidations.
exploit_steps: Flash loan stablecoins/DEI
Manipulate the DEI pool used as collateral price oracle
Exploit distorted collateral valuation to borrow/liquidate
Repay flash loans
Extract ~$13.4M and launder proceeds
invariant_broken: Collateral pricing must use a manipulation-resistant oracle independent of instantly-flash-loanable pool spot prices.
notes: Listed as 'Deus DAO (2)' on rekt leaderboard (04/28/2022, $13.4M) and DEUS Finance on DeFiLlama (flashloan price oracle attack). Distinct from the March 15 Deus incident. Detailed dedicated rekt post-mortem not separately verified; classification cross-confirmed by two index sources.

root_cause_short: Rari Fuse (Compound fork) CEther used call.value to send ETH before updating state; a malicious receiver re-entered exitMarket to withdraw collateral while keeping borrowed ETH.
exploit_steps: Flash loan 150M USDC and 50,000 WETH
Deposit 150M USDC as collateral into vulnerable fUSDC pool
Call borrow() to receive 1,977 ETH
borrow() sends ETH via call.value before recording debt
In the fallback, reenter and call exitMarket() to withdraw all collateral
Repeat across pools 8/18/27/127/144/146/156, repay flash loans, keep profit
invariant_broken: Borrow must record debt and finalize state before transferring ETH; a market cannot be exited while an unrecorded borrow is outstanding.
prerequisites: ETH transfer via call.value before state update
notes: Total ~$79.7M across seven Fuse pools; minor ~100 ETH follow-up on Arbitrum next day. A March-reported fix didn't cover exitMarket in Comptroller. ~5,400 ETH sent to Tornado Cash; Tribe DAO offered $10M no-questions bounty. Pattern shared with CREAM/Hundred/Voltage.

root_cause_short: A flaw in Saddle's metapool swap accounting allowed an attacker to extract value by swapping through the pool at mispriced rates.
exploit_steps: Enter Saddle metapool with sizable input
Exploit incorrect metapool swap/virtual-price accounting to receive disproportionate output
Cycle swaps to drain pool value
Exit with profit
invariant_broken: AMM swap accounting must preserve the pool invariant so no swap path returns more value than fairly priced.
notes: DeFiLlama classifies as 'Flashloan Swap Logic Exploit', ~$11M. Whitehats reportedly rescued a portion of funds (not independently verified here, left null). Dedicated rekt post-mortem slug not reachable during research.

root_cause_short: Fortress (Compound fork) combined a manipulable oracle with cheap governance, letting the attacker push a fake collateral price and borrow against it.
exploit_steps: Acquire governance power cheaply
Submit/pass a proposal or update setting a manipulated price for FTS collateral
Deposit overvalued collateral
Borrow and drain protocol assets
Launder proceeds
invariant_broken: Collateral price and governance-controlled parameters must not be cheaply manipulable to inflate borrowing power.
notes: DeFiLlama classifies as 'Governance and Oracle Exploit' (~$3M). rekt leaderboard lists Fortress Protocol 05/08/2022 $3M. Dedicated post-mortem not separately fetched; left details conservative.

root_cause_short: During the LUNA collapse, the Chainlink LUNA feed hit its minimum/froze while LUNA's real price crashed; Blizz/Venus kept valuing LUNA collateral at the stale price, letting attackers borrow against near-worthless LUNA.
exploit_steps: Acquire crashed LUNA cheaply on the open market
Deposit LUNA as collateral while the protocol oracle still reflects a far higher/floored price
Borrow all available assets against the overvalued collateral
Leave bad debt and exit with borrowed funds
invariant_broken: Collateral valuation must track real market price and halt borrowing when the oracle is stale or pinned at its floor.
prerequisites: oracle pinned at minimum / not updating
extreme real-price collapse of collateral asset
notes: DeFiLlama: 'Outdated Oracle Exploit', ~$21.8M (Blizz Finance + Venus on respective chains during UST/LUNA depeg). Primary chain shown as Avalanche per DeFiLlama for Blizz; Venus portion is BSC.

root_cause_short: Wintermute gave Optimism Foundation its mainnet Gnosis Safe address as the OP destination, but that address was uncontrolled on Optimism; because the original Safe used create (not create2), an attacker replayed deployments to claim the same address and seize 20M OP.
exploit_steps: 20M OP sent to an address Wintermute controlled on mainnet but not on Optimism
Identify that the Safe proxy was deployed via old ProxyFactory using the create opcode (address depends only on factory+nonce)
Run batched deployments (162 safes at a time) on Optimism, funded via Tornado Cash
Match the original nonce to deploy a proxy at the same address with attacker as owner
Take control of the 20M OP sitting at that address
invariant_broken: Funds must only be sent to addresses the recipient demonstrably controls on the target chain; counterfactual addresses must be non-replayable.
prerequisites: Safe deployed with create (nonce-based) not create2
tokens sent to uncontrolled address on a chain
notes: First of two Wintermute 2022 incidents. The exploiter returned the bulk of the OP to Wintermute afterward (widely reported); recovered amount left null pending exact figure.

root_cause_short: Second Inverse incident: attacker manipulated the price of a collateral token (yvCurve/CRV-based) feeding the oracle to borrow DOLA against inflated collateral.
exploit_steps: Flash loan large capital
Manipulate the underlying Curve/LP pool used to price the collateral token
Deposit overvalued collateral into Inverse
Borrow DOLA/assets against inflated value
Repay flash loan and exit with profit
invariant_broken: Collateral pricing must be resistant to flash-loan manipulation of the underlying liquidity pool.
prerequisites: oracle derived from manipulable LP spot price
notes: Second of two 2022 Inverse Finance incidents (~$5.8M). Detailed dedicated post-mortem not separately fetched; classification consistent with oracle manipulation per index sources.

root_cause_short: Harmony's Horizon bridge used a 2-of-5 multisig; two signer keys were compromised, giving full authority to drain the bridge.
exploit_steps: Compromise two of the five bridge multisig signer keys
From ~11:06 UTC, move 13.1k ETH from the ETH bridge to the exploiter address
Drain 5.5M BUSD and various ERC20s from the bridge
Route through secondary addresses and swap to ETH
On BSC also take 5k BNB and 640k BUSD
invariant_broken: Bridge withdrawals must require a sufficiently high signer threshold so that compromise of a small number of keys cannot move funds.
notes: Compromised signers 0xf845A7ee8477AD1FB4446651E548901a2635A915 and 0x812d8622C6F3c45959439e7ede3C580dA06f8f25. Later attributed by US/FBI to Lazarus (not in rekt source). A dev had publicly warned in April.

root_cause_short: Crema's fee-claim path failed to validate the owner of the tick account storing price/fee data; attacker supplied a fake tick account with fabricated fee data and claimed inflated fees.
exploit_steps: Create a fake tick account with fabricated fee data
Use flash loans to add liquidity to the protocol
Withdraw the liquidity
Claim inflated fees 'owed' per the fake tick data
Swap proceeds into 69,422.9 SOL and 6,497,738 USDCet (bridged to ETH)
invariant_broken: Accounts supplying fee/price data must be validated as protocol-owned before being trusted for payouts.
prerequisites: unvalidated owner on tick account in claim method
notes: Auditors caught the same flaw in swap method but missed it in claim method. Team offered $800k whitehat bounty (72h); attacker later returned funds (reported).

root_cause_short: Audius governance proxy stored its admin in slot 0, colliding with OpenZeppelin Initializable, letting the attacker re-initialize governance, fake voting power, and pass a treasury-draining proposal.
exploit_steps: Re-initialize the governance contract due to storage slot collision
Redefine voting params and set a new guardian address
Set governance address of Staking and DelegateManagerV2 to attacker contract
Create two fake 10-trillion AUDIO delegations to self
Pass a malicious proposal
Transfer 18,564,497 AUDIO from treasury to attacker, dump for ~704 ETH
invariant_broken: A deployed proxy's initializer must not be re-callable; admin storage must not collide with logic storage.
prerequisites: proxy admin in slot 0 colliding with Initializable
notes: Contracts previously audited by Kudelski and OpenZeppelin. Proceeds routed through Tornado Cash. Loss from treasury, not user funds.

root_cause_short: Attacker flash-loaned $10M from Solend to mint ANA and inflate its price on the bonding curve, then redeemed overvalued ANA against Nirvana's treasury.
exploit_steps: Flash loan $10M USDC from Solend
Use funds to mint ANA, pushing price from ~$8 to ~$24
Redeem the overvalued ANA against the Nirvana treasury for USDT
Net ~$3.5M profit on top of repaid loan
Bridge funds to Ethereum via Wormhole
invariant_broken: Treasury redemption price for ANA must not be inflatable within a single flash-loan transaction.
prerequisites: bonding-curve price responsive to instant mint
notes: Attacker Solana addr 76w4SBe2of2wWUsx2FjkkwD29rRznfvEkBa1upSbTAWH; ETH addr 0xb9ae2624ab08661f010185d72dd506e199e67c09. Docs had claimed 'ANA cannot go to zero'.

root_cause_short: A June Replica upgrade initialized the trusted root to 0x00, so any message (which hashes against 0x00 as the default) was treated as proven, letting anyone call process() to drain the bridge.
exploit_steps: Replica upgrade sets 0x00 as a trusted root
Craft a message whose value of 0 maps to the zero hash, accepted as a valid/proven root
Call process() directly, bypassing the prove step
Drain bridged assets
Copycats copy the exploit tx on Etherscan and swap in their own address
Hundreds participate (crowdhack), including whitehats and MEV bots, over ~2.5 hours
invariant_broken: A cross-chain message must only execute if its root was genuinely proven; the zero/default root must never be trusted.
prerequisites: Replica initialized with 0x00 as trusted root
notes: Permissionless 'crowdhack'; some addresses (e.g. claimed whitehats) later returned funds. Quantstamp's June audit (QSP-19) had foreshadowed a related issue. Significant whitehat returns occurred but exact total left null.

root_cause_short: The Slope mobile wallet transmitted users' seed phrases in plaintext to a centralized logging/telemetry server; an attacker who accessed those logs drained the affected wallets.
exploit_steps: Slope app sends user seed phrases to a centralized server in plaintext
Attacker obtains the logged mnemonics
Reconstruct private keys for affected wallets
Drain SOL and SPL tokens from ~9,231 wallets
invariant_broken: A non-custodial wallet must never transmit or store user seed phrases/private keys off-device in recoverable form.
prerequisites: access to Slope's logging server data
notes: Solana Foundation attributed the breach to Slope wallet software; ~9,231 wallets compromised, ~$8M across four collector addresses. DeFiLlama lists this as 'An Un-SOL-ved Mystery' / Save ~$5.3M; figures vary by source.

root_cause_short: Wintermute's hot wallet was a Profanity-generated vanity address; the tool's weak key generation let the private key be derived, and that address was still an authorized admin on the DeFi vault.
exploit_steps: Identify Wintermute's Profanity-generated vanity hot wallet
Exploit the Profanity vulnerability to derive the hot wallet's private key
Use the compromised key, still authorized as vault admin
Transfer funds out of the vault
Move ~$118M stablecoins into Curve 3pool plus WBTC/ETH
invariant_broken: Privileged keys must be generated with full entropy and revoked promptly when deprecated.
prerequisites: vanity address from vulnerable Profanity tool
notes: Second Wintermute 2022 incident. Profanity flaw was raised on GitHub in January. ~$118.4M stablecoins, 671 WBTC, 6,928 ETH. Wintermute had removed ETH from the admin address but forgot to remove it as vault admin.

root_cause_short: A flaw in the IAVL Merkle proof verification of the BSC Token Hub cross-chain precompile let the attacker forge a proof for a withdrawal that never occurred, minting 2M BNB.
exploit_steps: Identify the proof-verification flaw in the cross-chain Token Hub common library
Forge a low-level IAVL Merkle proof for a fabricated bridge withdrawal
Submit the forged proof to the precompile, which accepts it
Mint 2,000,000 BNB (two batches of 1M) to the attacker
Supply BNB on lending protocols and bridge a portion off-chain
invariant_broken: Cross-chain withdrawal proofs must be cryptographically verified so that no forged proof can authorize minting on the destination chain.
prerequisites: bug in IAVL/Merkle proof verification library
notes: BNB Chain validators halted the chain; most of the 2M BNB was frozen/kept under control, limiting realized loss (~$110-127M moved off-chain). rekt headline figure $586M = full 2M BNB; DeFiLlama ~$570M.

root_cause_short: Attacker manipulated the thin MNGO spot/perp market to inflate the value of a large long position, then used the inflated unrealized PnL as collateral to borrow and drain all lending pools.
exploit_steps: Fund address with >$5M USDC (sourced from FTX)
Open a large MNGO-PERP long on one account
Use a second account to pump MNGO spot from ~$0.03 to ~$0.91
Inflated mark price raises the long's unrealized profit/collateral
Borrow and withdraw all assets from Mango's lending pools (~$115M)
Trigger >4,000 short liquidations
invariant_broken: Borrowing power must not be derived from unrealized PnL marked at an easily manipulable, illiquid price.
prerequisites: protocol counts unrealized PnL as collateral
notes: Attacker later publicly identified as Avraham Eisenberg (not named in rekt source). Via governance he returned ~$67M, keeping ~$47M as a 'bounty'. He was later criminally charged. ~$70M had remained in treasury.

root_cause_short: TempleDAO's StaxLPStaking migrateStake function lacked validation of the caller-supplied staking contract, letting an attacker pass a malicious contract to withdraw staked LP tokens.
exploit_steps: Identify the unprotected migrateStake function
Call it supplying an attacker-controlled 'old staking' contract
Function trusts the malicious contract and credits/transfers the staked LP
Withdraw the LP tokens belonging to users
Exit with ~$2.3M
invariant_broken: Migration functions must validate that the supplied external contract is a trusted/whitelisted address before moving user funds.
prerequisites: migrateStake accepts arbitrary external staking contract
notes: rekt leaderboard lists TempleDAO 10/11/2022 $2.3M. Root cause (unvalidated migrateStake) is the widely documented technical cause; dedicated post-mortem not separately fetched, kept conservative.

root_cause_short: Moola (Aave fork on Celo) priced its low-liquidity MOO token via a manipulable feed; attacker pumped MOO and borrowed against the inflated collateral.
exploit_steps: Acquire MOO and deposit a base of stablecoins
Use part of the funds to pump the thin MOO market
Inflated MOO price raises collateral value
Borrow out CELO, cEUR, cUSD and other assets against overvalued MOO
Drain the lending pools
invariant_broken: Collateral for a low-liquidity governance token must use a manipulation-resistant price.
notes: On Celo (DeFiLlama lists chain Celo; not in enum, mapped chain_primary to ethereum-EVM family with chain=multi). Attacker returned the majority (~$8.4M of ~$9M) and kept a portion as a bounty per Moola's offer. Dedicated rekt post-mortem slug not reachable; classification cross-confirmed by two index sources.

root_cause_short: A flaw in Team Finance's Liquidity Locks migrate function (moving locked LP from Uniswap V2 to V3) let an attacker migrate to an attacker-controlled V3 pair at a skewed price and extract a large refund.
exploit_steps: Lock a token to the contract to bypass migrate validation
Invoke the migrate function transferring locked LP to a new attacker-controlled Uniswap V3 pair
Set a skewed price on the new pair
The skewed price yields a large refund/extraction
Withdraw ~$14.5-15.8M
invariant_broken: Liquidity migration must preserve value and validate destination pool/price so no refund exceeds the migrated value.
notes: Contract audited by Zokyo; migrate function reviewed but vuln missed. Loss ~$14.5M (Halborn) to ~$15.8M (rekt). Affected locked LP for several tokens.

root_cause_short: A flaw in Skyward's treasury/redemption accounting on NEAR let an attacker redeem SKYWARD against the treasury for more than its backing.
exploit_steps: Identify the redemption/treasury accounting flaw
Acquire SKYWARD tokens
Redeem them against the treasury exploiting the accounting mismatch
Drain treasury assets (~$3.2M)
Exit
invariant_broken: Token redemptions against the treasury must not pay out more than the redeemed tokens' backing.
notes: One of the few notable NEAR exploits in 2022 (~$3.2M, ~$3M DeFiLlama). DeFiLlama labels technique 'Reentrancy'; rekt leaderboard lists Skyward Finance 11/02/2022. Dedicated post-mortem not separately fetched; mechanics kept conservative.

root_cause_short: During FTX's collapse/bankruptcy filing, an unauthorized party with access to FTX wallet keys drained hot wallets across Ethereum and Solana; exact access method never publicly confirmed.
exploit_steps: Obtain access to FTX/FTX US hot wallet private keys (method unconfirmed)
Initiate mass outflows from FTX hot wallets on Ethereum and Solana
Swap stolen tokens (notably to ETH) to consolidate
Bridge Solana assets toward Ethereum
invariant_broken: Only authorized custodians should be able to sign withdrawals from exchange hot wallets.
notes: Only the technical on-chain drain is in scope (not the CeFi insolvency). rekt figure $477M; DeFiLlama ~$450M. Classified as private key compromise / unknown method. Some funds later linked in DOJ filings; attribution unconfirmed at incident time, left null.

root_cause_short: Ankr's BSC deployer key was compromised; the attacker upgraded the aBNBc token to a malicious implementation with an unrestricted mint function and minted ~60 trillion aBNBc, crashing the token and enabling downstream Helio borrowing.
exploit_steps: Compromise the Ankr deployer key (likely phishing)
Upgrade aBNBc to a malicious implementation
Use a hidden function bypassing caller checks to mint ~60 trillion aBNBc
Dump aBNBc into PancakeSwap pools for ~$5M
Separately, buy crashed aBNB cheaply and post as Helio collateral before its oracle updated
Borrow ~16M HAY (~$15.5M) before the price feed corrected
invariant_broken: Token minting must enforce caller authorization; upgradeable implementations must be protected by secure key custody; collateral oracles must reflect crashed prices promptly.
notes: ~$5M from Ankr aBNBc dump plus ~$15.5M + ~$3.5M extracted via Helio Money by opportunists. Audits by PeckShield and Beosin had flagged privileged-account risk. Binance froze ~$3M sent to the exchange.

root_cause_short: Lodestar's GLPOracle priced plvGLP without accounting for donate() to the GlpDepositor; an attacker donated to inflate the contract's assets and thus the plvGLP price, then borrowed against inflated collateral.
exploit_steps: Flash loan capital
Call donate() on the GlpDepositor to inflate its asset balance
GLPOracle reports an inflated plvGLP price not adjusted for the donation
Deposit plvGLP as overvalued collateral
Borrow out all supplied funds (~$6.5M)
Repay flash loan, swap to ETH, bridge to mainnet
invariant_broken: Collateral price for plvGLP must not be inflatable by direct donations to the underlying depositor.
notes: Compound fork on Arbitrum. ~2.8M GLP (~$2.4M) noted recoverable. Attack ETH (~343, ~$430k) had been bridged from Polygon ~3 months earlier. rekt ~$6.5M; DeFiLlama ~$6.9M.

root_cause_short: Raydium's pool-owner/admin private key was compromised (suspected trojan), letting the attacker drain accumulated pool fees and inflate withdrawals via the withdraw_pnl path.
exploit_steps: Compromise the pool owner/admin private key (suspected trojan)
Sign as admin to drain pools without holding/burning LP tokens
Withdraw accumulated trading/protocol fees via withdraw_pnl
Modify the SyncNeedTake parameter to inflate expected fees and withdraw extra funds
Bridge most proceeds to Ethereum, swap to ETH, deposit to Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Privileged pool-owner authority must be securely custodied; fee withdrawals must be bounded by genuine accrued fees.
notes: OtterSec attributed to compromised key/trojan. Affected SOL-USDC, SOL-USDT, RAY pools and others. ~100k SOL (~$1.4M) remained on Solana. Team halted authority and patched.

root_cause_short: Defrost's V1 was drained when a fake collateral token with a manipulated price oracle was added (via owner privileges), triggering improper liquidations; widely flagged as a rug-pull-style backdoor.
exploit_steps: Add a malicious fake LSDCRV collateral token with attacker-controlled price oracle
Set a manipulated price for the fake collateral
Use the fake price to liquidate legitimate positions
Seize users' collateral
Extract ~$6M
invariant_broken: New collateral tokens and price oracles must not be addable by a single privileged key without controls; liquidation prices must come from trusted feeds.
prerequisites: owner can add arbitrary collateral and oracle
notes: DeFiLlama classifies as Rugpull/Oracle Manipulation, ~$6M. Initially accused of exit scam; team later claimed hack and reportedly returned funds (recovery amount not verified, left null). Included per scope (rug pull WITH technical backdoor).

root_cause_short: BonqDAO trusted Tellor spot price values for WALBT collateral; an attacker who staked only 10 TRB gained price-reporting rights and submitted an arbitrary price.
exploit_steps: Stake ~10 TRB (~$175) in TellorFlex to obtain reporter rights
Call submitValue to massively inflate the WALBT collateral price
Mint 100M BEUR stablecoin against 0.1 WALBT in the same window
In a second tx, submit an extremely low WALBT price
Liquidate other users' troves, capturing ~113M WALBT
Swap loot and bridge proceeds to Ethereum / Tornado Cash
invariant_broken: Collateral valuation must use a manipulation-resistant (time-averaged / multi-source) price, not a single attacker-controllable spot report.
prerequisites: Ability to become a Tellor reporter with minimal stake
notes: Theoretical mintable value was ~$120M but the attacker only realized ~$1.7M (711 ETH + 535k DAI). AllianceBlock reissued ALBT and airdropped to victims.
